answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog post (NVIDIA Blog, title 'NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout'), published and event-dated 2026-07-01; tier party_statement. It carries a quoted statement from Sharon AI's CEO, reproduced by NVIDIA, and NVIDIA's description of a Firmus project.
answer.note: Source claim: NVIDIA says a new business model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, using a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure. Under this structure, NVIDIA would earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which NVIDIA describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This is a company description of a model being introduced, not a reported financial result, so it supports the business description and the intended revenue channels rather than any amount, margin or timing. Partner evidence is weaker: Sharon AI's CEO statement describes a collaboration and sovereign AI compute mission without terms, and NVIDIA's statement that AI clouds are building DSX AI factories is a general description. Firmus's Batam campus is a stated expectation ('expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs'), so it is a plan with no completion date, funding or contract status given. Conditional reading: if the revenue-share and credit-support model is implemented as described, NVIDIA's revenue mix could include a usage-linked cloud revenue share and some financing exposure through credit support, with the scale of both unknown from this source. The source also names AI natives (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) as demand examples, which show the target customer category but not NVIDIA sales to them.
limitations: The source gives no quantified revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount, contract duration or accounting treatment for the NVIDIA model, so its financial size cannot be estimated from it.
The Firmus 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are expectations with no stated completion date, financing status or confirmed NVIDIA supply contract, so they do not establish NVIDIA orders or shipments.
Sharon AI's statement gives no terms, capacity size or signing status for its collaboration with NVIDIA.
The source does not state whether any named AI cloud has signed an agreement under the new model; that status is unknown, not confirmed as absent.
Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI are named only as examples of demand; the source does not say they buy NVIDIA infrastructure through this model or in what amount.
The statement is a company-published description; no independent confirmation of the model's rollout or uptake is in the supplied records.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next annual report (10-K) and subsequent quarterly filings for disclosure of revenue-share arrangements, credit guarantees or financing commitments tied to AI cloud partners.
Search for signed or announced agreements between NVIDIA or named AI clouds (Sharon AI, Firmus) under this model and any disclosed capacity, value or completion dates.
Check Firmus and Sharon AI public filings or announcements for the Batam campus schedule, power and financing status, and any NVIDIA supply terms.
